subject: Dedicated GPU pool sizing & pricing — Atlas Health
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@atlashealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing & pricing for Dedicated GPU pool

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this. We’re evaluating Dedicated capacity at Redwood for an upcoming conversational assistant used across our clinician portal and patient intake flows. A few details on our expected workload so you can recommend a pool size and reserved-commit structure: 

- Avg requests: ~60 req/s sustained during business hours (08:00–20:00 UTC-7), spikes up to ~120 req/s for brief windows (5–10 minutes).
- Typical prompt/context: ~1k tokens (system + history + user), but some long cases up to 4k tokens.
- Concurrency: we expect steady concurrency of 80–100 during peaks; backend can accept queueing up to 200 concurrent websocket sessions.
- Model target: we want a high-quality 70B-ish open model (you previously suggested Redwood-70B-v2 or equivalent).
- Availability: 99.9% monthly availability and a throughput SLA is important for our SREs.

Please include: recommended pool (GPU type & count), expected throughput and latency targets (p50/p95), suggested reserved commits (monthly hours/discount tiers), and any recommended optimizations (quant, batching, cache). Also, what discounts do you typically offer for a 12–24 month reserved commit?

Appreciate a rough proposal by EOW.

Regards,
Carlos
Director of Product — Atlas Health
[Attachment: workload_sample_log.json (JSON, 235KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Hi Carlos — thanks for the details, this is exactly the level we need. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I put numbers together: 

1) Are the 60 req/s and 120 spike numbers measured in user requests or generation/token-stream events? (i.e., does a single request translate to a single generation call?)
2) Are p99 latency targets important, or is p95 sufficient for your SRE SLA?
3) Do you have a 30-minute sample of production traffic we can run through our sizing sheet? The workload_sample_log is a great start.

I’ll assemble an initial recommended pool and two reserved-commit options (12m / 24m) and share a draft SOW + sizing sheet by Thu. If you’re free, let’s also book a 30-min walkthrough on Thu afternoon.

Best,
Jordan Blake

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Atlas Health — need sizing + pricing recommendation

Team — forwarding Atlas Health’s workload notes. Key asks: recommended GPU pool (type & count) for 24/7 reserved pool that handles 60 req/s sustained, 120 req/s spiky, context length up to 4k, target model ~70B, throughput SLA desired. They also asked about discount bands for 12–24m commits.

Can you propose: 1) conservative pool (no autoscale) 2) autoscale-enabled pool with burst capacity 3) suggested pricing bands (monthly commit + discount) and how we justify the SLA. I’ve attached their sample log.

Thanks — Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas Health — need sizing + pricing recommendation

Jordan / Rishi / Laura — reviewed the sample and ran a few sims. Summary recommendation below (high level):

1) Recommended pool (production):
- GPU target: 8 x A100-80GB (or equivalent NVLink-enabled 80GB-class accelerators). Rationale: workload typical context ~1k tokens; peaks up to 4k require larger memory to keep KV cache warm for low latency.
- Throughput: ~70–80 req/s sustained with p95 < 220ms for Redwood-70B-v2 quantized path when using continuous batching. With burst window and queueing, system can absorb 120 req/s for 5–10 minutes with p95 moving to ~400ms.
- Concurrency headroom: supports ~100 concurrent active requests at target latency; recommend configuring queue depth for short spikes.

2) Autoscale / burst proposal:
- Base reserved pool: 8 GPUs (24/7 commit).
- Burst capacity: add 4 GPUs on demand for short windows (pre-warmed hot pool). Autoscale policy: add when standing queue > 40 for more than 30s, remove when queue < 10 for 3m.

3) Reserved commit recommendations & pricing bands (ballpark):
- 12-month commit: commit for 8 GPUs constant — list price equivalent to $X/hour (internal pricing sheet attached). Typical discount: 23%–28% off hosted rates for 12m.
- 24-month commit: 8 GPUs + 4 GPU burst — deeper discount: 30%–38% (depends on enterprise add-ons, e.g., extended retention/priority support).
- Alternative structure: commit to a monthly GPU-hour minimum (e.g., 8 * 24 * 30 hours) + overage rate — useful if they want flexibility to scale down non-peak periods.

4) SLA & guarantees:
- We can offer a throughput SLA tied to committed pool (e.g., baseline throughput guarantee for committed capacity; failover to hosted variants if capacity is constrained).
- Operational SLOs: 99.9% up for Dedicated control plane; routing fallbacks documented in SOW. Penalty/credit structure to be negotiated (suggest 5% service credit per 0.1% breach after a threshold).

5) Optimization levers to reduce pool size/cost:
- Quantization + int8 kernel where acceptable to reduce memory/compute per token.
- Prefix/KV caching for frequent prompts (can reduce effective tokens served).
- Request routing to smaller model variants for low-sensitivity traffic.
- Intelligent batching windows tuned to their latency envelope (we simulated 16–32ms batching window).

6) Recommended next steps:
- Share a cleaned sizing sheet with cost scenarios (I attached a working sheet).
- Offer a 30-day pilot: 25% off for the pilot month with a performance baseline measurement clause.

I’ll drop numbers into the pricing sheet and propose two commercial options for Jordan to present: (A) 12m conservative, (B) 24m with burst and pilot.

— Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: gpu_pool_sizing_sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 64KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing & pricing for Dedicated GPU pool

Carlos — thanks for the patience. Based on our sims (attached) here are two concrete options for Atlas Health:

Option A — 12-month reserved commit (conservative)
- Baseline: 8 x A100-80GB GPUs, 24/7 reserved pool.
- Performance: ~70–80 req/s sustained; p95 latency target ~220ms on Redwood-70B-v2 quantized path. Handles 120 req/s bursts for up to 10 minutes with p95~400ms.
- Pricing: Monthly commit = equivalent of $XX,XXX / month (list), ~25% discount off hosted list.
- Trial: add-on 30-day pilot (single-month billing) at 25% off to validate performance.

Option B — 24-month reserved commit (preferred economics)
- Baseline: 8 x A100-80GB + 4 x burst GPUs (pre-warmed). Autoscale policy included.
- Performance: same baseline; burst reduces p95 during short spikes to ~300ms.
- Pricing: Monthly commit = $YY,YYY / month (list), ~34% discount off hosted list + additional operational SLA commitments. Includes 1 month free within the first year (pro-rated).

SLA notes: we can commit to an availability SLO for the Dedicated control plane (99.9%). Throughput SLA will be tied to the committed pool; we propose a performance baseline measurement period (30 days) before SLA takes effect.

Next steps: I attached a draft SOW and the detailed sizing sheet. If acceptable, we can:
1) Kick off a 30-day pilot (option A pricing) to gather live telemetry.
2) If pilot meets p95/p50 baselines, convert to the reserved commit with agreed discount and SOW terms.

Would you be available Thurs 11am PDT for a 30-min call to review?

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: SOW-Dedicated-AtlasHealth-v2.pdf (PDF, 145KB); gpu_pool_sizing_sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 64KB)]

From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@atlashealth.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing & pricing for Dedicated GPU pool

Jordan — thanks for the clear options. A few follow-ups from procurement / product: 

- Discount: 34% on the 24m option is compelling, but procurement needs another 6% to hit internal cap. Would Redwood be able to flex to 40% if we commit to a 24-month term and include enterprise add-ons (longer log retention + priority support)?
- SLA: we need the throughput SLA to specify p95 generation latency <= 200ms for baseline traffic measured after the pilot. Can we commit to that?
- Pilot: we appreciate the 30-day pilot offer. Can we get the pilot priced as credited toward the first committed month (i.e., if we convert, the pilot cost is credited back)?

If you can confirm the above, we’ll route for legal + procurement next week.

Best,
Carlos
Director of Product — Atlas Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Atlas Health — supplier discount request (40%) / SLA ask

Looping in Laura and Marissa — Atlas is pushing for 40% on 24m if we include extended retention + priority support; also wants p95 <= 200ms baseline after pilot and pilot credited toward committed month. Procurement will route to legal if we confirm commercials.

Can we approve a one-time commercial concession: additional 6% for 24m if we get enterprise add-ons (which increase ARR) and include pilot-credit (convert pilot cost to first-month credit)? Also need confirmation from Marissa that the p95 <= 200ms is achievable with the 8+4 burst config post-pilot.

Jordan
